title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
slides: A hacker breached John Deere using AI agents — why them?

The agents chained exploits without a human in the loop
Your perimeter may already be scanned by autonomous bots
Check one exposed endpoint today — before an agent finds it
thread_text:
1. AI agents hacked John Deere

A hacker used autonomous AI agents to breach the agriculture giant. The same tactic later hit SharkNinja in a separate campaign. Welcome to the new attack surface.

2. Why John Deere first?

Because a manufacturer with legacy systems and a huge digital footprint is a perfect target for automated scanning. The agents didn't need a human to chain exploits.

3. No human in the loop

The AI agents chained multiple exploits together without any human intervention. That means the attack happened faster than your security team could even detect it.

4. Your perimeter is already scanned

Autonomous bots are already probing exposed endpoints across the internet. If you haven't checked your own attack surface, someone else's agent already has.

5. Check one exposed endpoint today

Pick a public-facing service and verify it's patched and monitored. If an AI agent can find it, it will. Do it now, before the next campaign starts.
